osNotes.darwin: The descriptor path is measured on Linux only. fstat/fchmod/ftruncate and the cursor read-back go through /proc/self/fd and /proc/self/fdinfo, which darwin does not have; fd-io.ts falls back to acting on the PATH there, and tellFd() to sizeOfFd(). Both fallbacks are gated on the measured CAN_PROC_FD capability rather than assumed, but no darwin host has run them — shipping an unmeasured darwin path is how the first cut of this work shipped a broken umask probe. The O_* table in posix-flags.ts carries darwin values (O_CREAT 0x200 collides with Linux O_TRUNC, which is why it is host-keyed at all) and those are equally unexercised: prebuilds.yml runs no darwin leg for this package. copyFileSync additionally branches on isDarwin(): the kernel write-time privilege strip is not portable — Linux's should_remove_suid() keeps S_ISGID without S_IXGRP, XNU strips it either way (measured on both macOS legs, 2644 -> 0644 vs 2644 -> 2644). Node inherits that for free because the kernel does the stripping; we spell it. watch-tree.ts branches on isDarwin() a second time, for fs.watch: a Gio DIRECTORY monitor here reports a child being created or deleted but never a write landing inside an existing child (measured through a raw Gio.FileMonitor on both macOS legs; the probe is watch-backend.gjs.spec.ts and stays in the suite), so every watched FILE is given a monitor of its own. That is not a recursion feature -- a flat fs.watch(dir, cb) needs it too, or a rewrite of dir/config.json produces no event at all. The residual gap, and why this stays partial: the fan-out grows one monitor per FILE where Node's FSEvents stream costs one subscription for the whole tree, so it is BOUNDED -- a watch over a tree larger than the budget raises ERR_FS_WATCH_MONITOR_BUDGET naming the limit and the path it stopped at, and is incomplete from there on. What one monitor costs the kernel here is NOT established: the macOS legs report a soft RLIMIT_NOFILE of 1048575 and a descriptor delta of zero across 27 monitors, so the budget bounds growth without claiming to ration descriptors.
osNotes.win32: Not attempted. The implementation is POSIX open(2)/mkdir(2) semantics with real O_CREAT|O_EXCL, an fd-owned cursor and mode-at-creation; win32 has no procfs, no POSIX mode bits and different open flags. The WIN32 branch in posix-flags.ts exists so the table is total, not because the package works there — the fs specs already carry `it.failing({ when: isWin32() })` rows saying the same.
